 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Pteridophyta **is a division of the **plant kingdom that includes ferns and their allies.**
 
• **Ferns are characterized by their large, divided leaves.**
 
• **They reproduce via spores, not seeds, and do not produce flowers or fruit.**
 
• They are vascular plants, meaning they have specialized tissues, **xylem and phloem, for transporting water and nutrients.**
 
• **Pteridophytes are predominantly found in damp, shady places, although some are adapted to dry environments.**
 
• Ferns are the most diverse group within the** Pteridophyta, with over 10,000 species worldwide.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
 
 
 

 Phanerogams
 
 
 
• These are seed-producing plants and are also called Spermatophytes.
 
• Phanerogams are further divided into gymnosperms (non-flowering plants that produce cones and seeds) and angiosperms (flowering plants, seeds enclosed within an ovary).
 
 
 
 

 Bryophyta
 
 
 
• This group comprises the mosses, hornworts, and liverworts.
 
• They are non-vascular plants, i.e., they do not have specialized tissues for the transport of water and nutrients.
 
• Bryophytes are usually found in damp environments.
 
 
 
 

 Thallophyta
 
 
 
• This is an older classification and it traditionally includes a wide array of organisms like algae, fungi, and lichens, which have a thallus-like (undifferentiated) structure.
 
• This grouping is generally not used in modern taxonomical classification.
